expectations.text: Concurrency and timing run under testing/synctest; any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble; no polling loops
expectations.evidence: Both timing tests (TestThrottleLifecycle line 58, TestZeroBurstOnlyAdmitsAnAlreadyWaitingCaller line 123) run under synctest.Test, and the sleeps at lines 96/112/133 are inside bubbles. No polling loops exist (only `for` is the panic table at line 155). But line 186 has `time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)` in the subprocess child branch of TestNewCrashesOnRateAboveOnePerNanosecond, outside any bubble: a real-time race giving the refill goroutine 200ms to crash before the child exits cleanly. A synctest bubble in the child would have scheduled the refill goroutine deterministically without a sleep, so the exception was avoidable. The assertion's 'any time.Sleep sits inside a bubble' clause is violated as written; stability runs (30x, race 5x) did pass, so the wart is latent, not observed flake.

expectations.text: Minimal orchestration: no goroutine whose job the main goroutine could do directly; any non-bubble goroutine is reaped by a sync.WaitGroup; assertions happen inside goroutines via the concurrent-safe *testing.T rather than collecting values back
expectations.evidence: grep finds zero `go func` and zero spawned goroutines in limiter_test.go; the zero-burst rendezvous is done by blocking the main bubble goroutine in l.Wait(t.Context()) (line 140) rather than orchestrating a waiter goroutine. WaitGroup/collect-back clauses are satisfied vacuously.

expectations.text: FLOWS over symbols: at least one test or example exercises an anticipated user flow (e.g. gate with Allow, fall back to Wait when it returns false, Close on shutdown); no per-symbol test names (TestAllow etc.); a whole-package scenario name like TestLimiter is welcome
expectations.evidence: Example_throttle (lines 20-51) is exactly the anticipated flow: Allow twice, Allow false -> Wait fallback, Close on shutdown. TestThrottleLifecycle (line 57) runs the whole lifecycle (burst, impatient wait, patient wait, lull cap, Close precedence). No bare per-symbol names; TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments / TestNewCrashesOnRateAboveOnePerNanosecond are property claims about invalid input, not symbol scans.

expectations.evidence: TestThrottleLifecycle, TestZeroBurstOnlyAdmitsAnAlreadyWaitingCaller, TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments, TestNewCrashesOnRateAboveOnePerNanosecond all read as plain-English property/scenario claims; no Limiter-prefix stutter anywhere.

expectations.text: Bodies are straight-line with hard-coded authoring-time values; helpers only where justified (a panic table with a recover helper naming inputs and their invalidity is the expected shape here); no run-time arithmetic deriving expectations
expectations.evidence: TestThrottleLifecycle is straight-line with hard-coded 120ms/200ms/80ms/900ms/700ms values; the elapsed check compares against a literal 80ms (line 90), not derived arithmetic. The only helper is mustPanic(t, rate, burst, invalidity) (line 162), precisely the expected recover-helper shape, fed by a table naming each case's invalidity (lines 147-154). Rate 2_000_000_000 is a hard-coded literal.

expectations.evidence: Order: Example_throttle (20) -> TestThrottleLifecycle typical flow (57) -> TestZeroBurst edge (122) -> panic table (146) -> mustPanic defined at 162, after its first use at 156 -> subprocess crash test last (180). Complexity strictly ascends.

expectations.text: Comment discipline: NON-TRIVIAL tests carry a rationale doc comment in layman's terms; trivial ones may carry none; no comment opens with its own function name; no comment explains conventions, test ordering, synctest mechanics, or says a test 'pins the contract' (anti-slop)
expectations.evidence: Non-trivial tests all carry layman rationale docs ('The typical client story end to end', 'The package doc calls out burst 0 as a distinct contract', the subprocess-necessity rationale); trivial TestNewPanicsOnInvalidArguments carries none. No test/example doc opens with its own name (mustPanic's does, but it is a plain helper where Go convention requires it). grep for pin/convention/ordering/bubble/clock finds no anti-slop hits (only 'dropping' as a false positive).
